messages:
nala: Quick sync: proposal for a tiny edge-first canary escape hatch. Goals: fast fail, tenant-scoped, cheap decisions, and auditable events. Thoughts? :thinking:

ben: +1. Core idea: edge fetches a small policy blob, runs a timered evaluator (not per-request), and sets an in-memory override for the tenant when signals exceed thresholds. Use EWMA smoothing and short TTL.

omar: Main risks: split-brain across nodes and autoscaler churn. Mitigations: override TTL (e.g., 30s), backoff ladder before re-eval, require N healthy ticks to recover, and per-tenant scope by default.

nala: Policy sketch:
{"schema":"edge-escape-v1","scope":"tenant","ewma_alpha":0.18,"threshold":0.05,"ttl_s":30,"recover_ticks":3,"backoff_s":[30,60,120],"force_key":"console.override.v1"}

ben: Observability: emit metric edge_override_total{reason,tenant,instance} and add trace header x-edge-fallback: inst=...,reason=...,policy_rev=... when applied. Also push stamped telemetry event on change.

omar: Ownership: infra owns synthetic probes and EWMA infra; runtime owns feature checks (hallucination detectors). Policy should combine signals with configurable weights.

infra-bot: [deploy-check] edge-escape-v1 schema lint OK. Suggest adding min_evaluate_interval_s for noisy clusters.

nala: Action items: ben to prototype evaluator + TTL/backoff (PR); infra to publish probe ownership doc and EWMA lib; omar to design trace header + metrics. Keep schema compatible with Dedicated by allowing control-plane-sourced policy. :white_check_mark:
